rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (entityR2A, 60 trials, score 625.2): the oval finished 20 of 20 at a mean of 1.95 s, which is well inside the 3 s limit. The s-bend finished 17 of 20 (progress 0.97) but its steering_oscillation was high at 0.42. The slalom failed on every trial (progress 0.17, off_track, max_error about 0.0615 m, one line-loss event per run), and its oscillation was 0.15, which is at the Evaluator's threshold. The failure is an early drift off the line on the slalom, not jitter. Iteration 1 (kp 1.2) and iteration 2 (kp 1.4) both stopped the slalom at about 17% progress, so the robot is not holding the line through the slalom's sharp direction changes at these gains. Following the Evaluator's rule for low-jitter off-track failures, this candidate raises kp from 1.4 to 1.6 and keeps kd at 0.4 and base_speed at 1.0. The kp step should give a stronger correction on the slalom. Keeping kd at 0.4 avoids adding damping on top of the change, so the race isolates the kp effect. Geometry is unchanged, so any change in the result comes from the controller. Expected result: slalom progress rises above 0.17 and some runs finish, with max_error below 0.06 m and line_loss_events falling toward zero. Oval should still finish under 2.2 s. Risk: the s-bend oscillation (0.42) may rise with kp. If it does, the next step is kd toward 0.5 with kp held at 1.6. Hypotheses to check: (1) kp 1.6 should reduce slalom off-track events; (2) if s-bend oscillation rises above 0.5 while the robot stays on the line, kd is the limiting term; (3) if the oval completion time rises above 3 s, base_speed is too low. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors, and noise_robustness, all per track.
